dataset_family: Tehran Geriatric Eye Study (TGES), population-based stratified random cluster sample of residents aged 60+ in Tehran, Iran, 2019; 1,190 analysed of 3,310 participants (299 MMSE-defined MCI, 891 normal)
method_family: Clinical optometric near point of convergence (push-up target, ruler, mean of five measurements) as a vergence/binocular-vision measure; simple, age-sex and multivariable logistic regression plus ROC
what_it_shows: Within its own sample, NPC was more receded in MMSE-defined MCI than in cognitively normal participants (10.89 vs 7.76 cm, P<0.001). The association survived adjustment for age, BMI, diabetes, stroke, education and refraction (OR 1.334 per cm, 95% CI 1.263-1.410). NPC alone gave AUC 0.764 at a cut-off of >8.5 cm (sensitivity 70.9%, specificity 69.5%), with the cut-off derived and evaluated in the same data.
why: PDF identity confirmed: title, authors (Doostdar, Hashemi, Nabovati, Asharlous, Khabazkhoob) and Int J Ophthalmol 2023;16(4):623-629 match the block. STATED FORM: partly, and conditional on a scope decision the verifier cannot make alone. NPC is an ocular channel, and the paper frames it through vergence eye-movement control (p.5). But it is a single clinical threshold of maximal convergence, measured by examiner push-up with a ruler, not recorded eye-movement behaviour of the kind in P-966 (saccades on a tracker). If the operator rules that 'eye-movement behaviour' excludes clinical vergence measures, both verdicts become 'no'. On the study's own data, the MCI-versus-normal comparison, the adjusted OR and the AUC are real and in the stated direction. Limits: (1) MCI is defined only as MMSE 18-23, with no clinical adjudication. The MCI group had about half the schooling of the normal group (5.15 vs 10.26 years, Table 1), and MMSE is education-sensitive, so the label partly reflects education. In the study's favour, adjusting for education barely moved the OR (simple 1.352, age-sex 1.354, multivariable 1.334). (2) The AUC is for NPC alone, unadjusted and in-sample, and the 8.5 cm threshold was not validated. (3) It is cross-sectional, and the authors concede that direction is unknown and that only a single global cognitive test was used. (4) Heavy exclusions (for example 751 for intraocular surgery, 585 for BCVA/ocular disease, 294 for dementia or MMSE<18, 300 for missing data) leave 1,190 of 3,310 participants, a selected subset of the population sample. SCALABLE: of the four candidates it comes closest, as a routine low-cost optometric test in a population-based sample, but no screening deployment was tested. The authors' recommendation that people with NPC>8.5 cm be referred for cognitive screening is a proposal. NARROWED FORM: partly. It shows a preliminary, unvalidated association of an ocular measure with MCI, matching the narrowed wording's head clause. But it is population-based rather than single-centre, and it is neither retinal imaging nor a saccadic measure. Admitting it would require the narrowed wording to add a vergence (NPC) channel, with MCI defined by MMSE only. INDEPENDENCE: Tehran/IUMS/Noor authors and the TGES sample share nothing with P-5, P-105, P-952 or P-966, or with the other candidates (P-169 Hanyang, P-282 Mayo, P-363 Duke). Not a preprint.
